findings.claim: PARTIAL closure: the revised prescribed G pairs are distinguishable, but the matrix still lacks a dedicated target/mutant for filtering J by job.run_id. Selecting the correct run R and selecting jobs belonging to R are separate predicates. Removing only the latter survives all 23 G targets; the specification therefore still does not require proof of every new H2 guard.

observed: All 23 G input variants pass the actual current-master kiem-merge CLI: rc=0, empty stderr. A reference implementation of the written H2 predicates gives khac for each correct target and du (G01-G17) or dich (G18-G23) under its prescribed mutant. These are contract-feasibility probes, not execution of a future B4 implementation.

In the same reference predicate, deleting only the J run_id comparison leaves the result khac on every one of those 23 targets. G01/G04/G05/G06 retain eight skipped jobs in the correct run; combining them with foreign full jobs creates duplicate shard names, so the uniqueness guard still rejects. G02 changes attempt, not run identity. The other G targets do not mix runs.

A separate counterexample keeps the five required K2 jobs in selected ci.yml run 100, puts no G5 shards in that run, and puts eight successful full-G5 shards with matching H/attempt in unrelated workflow run 99. Actual current CLI returns rc=0. Correct H2 returns khac; deleting only the J run_id filter returns du. With --siet-g5-du this is precisely the missing red-to-green distinction.
The table contains 88 unique row IDs and no row assigning that independent J-filter fault a target. Raw observations are in h2-results.json.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a dedicated matrix row using the demonstrated layout: selected CI run retains its five required jobs but no G5 shards; another run supplies eight full shards with the same H/attempt. Under --siet-g5-du, require K0-K7 green and only K2b red; a mutant removing only the J run_id comparison must make that exact target raise ChotB4. Keep the existing R-selection and attempt cases, update row/mutant counts and estimates, and retain target-specific false-credit checks. Do not repair this by broadening accepted job provenance or borrowing a duplicate-name failure; those would hide the missing guard.

findings.claim: PARTIAL closure: ADR-0053 activation and the five-file delivery inventory are now explicit, but nang_tran is still not compliant with the literal exception contract. Its can_cu explicitly has no measured numstat, while ai_nang makes the 4,000-added-line exception effective on approval of this spec hash and the process copies that unchanged block into the installing Mission revision and lease. Measuring later before code review does not supply the evidence required in the approved spec/lease.

findings.suggested_fix: Revise Kích thước and the pre-lease process so this estimate does not grant an effective exception. A viable approach is B1 r3’s sequence: separately budget/authorize a representative scratch sizing build, measure the complete five-file delivery diff against its exact baseline, place that numstat and the non-splitting rationale into a subsequent approved spec revision, then copy the measured block into Mission/lease. Alternatively obtain an explicit owner disposition changing the ADR evidence requirement; ordinary spec-hash approval is not such a stated disposition. Before source review, remeasure against the approved cap. Preserve every acceptance target and mutant; the fix must not create an unbudgeted author call or shrink coverage to fit 450 lines.

findings.claim: Acceptance 2 does not partition its required fixture population completely. Four existing _c1106 cases reject an invalid lease before K2 runs. They are neither K2-red, nor K2-passed/base-red, nor base-passed, so the three frozen A/B categories give no result rule for them. Treating absence of a K2 failure as K2 passed would incorrectly require new K2b output on these early exits, conflicting with unchanged argument handling and the ban on changing old expectations.

observed: Ran the actual existing cases cong_c_k1_anchor, cong_c_k1_yaml_hong, cong_c_k1_khoa_trung and cong_c_k1_tag_hong against current master. All four case assertions passed; each child CLI returned rc=2, empty stdout, and only a lease-parser error on stderr. No K2 failure or K2b output exists.

cmd_kiem_merge parses and rejects the lease before defining/executing its K0-K7 checks. Thus K2 is not_run on these cases, not passed. All four actually call _c1106 and belong to acceptance 1’s population, which acceptance 2 reuses without exclusion.
Raw child outputs, including the four distinct parser diagnostics, are saved in early-exit-results.json. The original B4-S01 projection correction does not define this additional early-exit category.

findings.suggested_fix: Extend acceptance 2 with an explicit early-rejection category, or expand (a) to cover K2 not_run as well as K2 failed: require identical rc/stdout/stderr and zero K2b diagnostics, with no projection. Enumerate these four existing cases in the A/B population and add comparator self-checks accepting their unchanged outputs and rejecting an added LAN_G5/K2b line or a changed parser diagnostic. Preserve argument-validation order and existing tests; distinguish not_run from passed instead of inferring success merely from absence of a THIẾU K2 line.
